§ 10.01 TITLE OF CODE.
   (A)   All ordinances of a permanent and general nature of the county, as
revised, codified, rearranged, renumbered and consolidated into component
codes, titles, chapters and sections, shall be known and designated as the
“Morrow County Code,” for which designation “code of ordinances,” “codified
ordinances” or “code” may be substituted. Code title, chapter and section
headings do not constitute any part of the law as contained in the code.
   (B)   All references to codes, titles, chapters and sections are to the
components of the code unless otherwise specified. Any component code may be
referred to and cited by its name, such as the “Traffic Code.” Sections may be
referred to and cited by the designation “§” followed by the number, such as “§
10.01.” Headings and captions used in this code other than the title, chapter
and section numbers are employed for reference purposes only and shall not be
deemed a part of the text of any section.
§ 10.02 INTERPRETATION.
   Unless otherwise provided herein, or by law or implication required, the
same rules of construction, definition and application shall govern the
interpretation of this code as those governing the interpretation of state law.
§ 10.03 APPLICATION TO FUTURE ORDINANCES.
   All provisions of Title I compatible with future legislation shall apply to
ordinances hereafter adopted amending or supplementing this code unless
otherwise specifically provided.
§ 10.04 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   General rule. Words and phrases shall be taken in their plain, or
ordinary and usual sense. However, technical words and phrases having a
peculiar and appropriate meaning in law shall be understood according to their
technical import.
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this code, the following definitions
shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      BUSINESS DAY. Any 24-hour day other than a Saturday, Sunday or federal or
state legal holiday.
      CODE, THIS CODE or THIS CODE OF ORDINANCES. This municipal code as
modified by amendment, revision and adoption of new titles, chapters or
sections.
      COUNTY. Morrow County, Oregon.
      DAY. Calendar day unless otherwise indicated as business day or working
day.
      GOVERNING BODY. The County Board of Commissioners.
      MAY. The act referred to is permissive.
      MONTH. A calendar month.
      OATH. An affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be
substituted for an oath, and in such cases the words SWEAR and SWORN shall be
equivalent to the words AFFIRM and AFFIRMED.
      OFFICER, OFFICE, EMPLOYEE, COMMISSION or DEPARTMENT. An officer, office,
employee, commission or department of this county unless the context clearly
requires otherwise.
      PERSON. Extends to and includes person, persons, firm, corporation,
copartnership, trustee, lessee or receiver. Whenever used in any clause
prescribing and imposing a penalty, the terms PERSON or WHOEVER as applied to
any unincorporated entity shall mean the partners or members thereof, and as
applied to corporations, the officers or agents thereof.
      PRECEDING or FOLLOWING. Next before or next after, respectively.
      SHALL. The act referred to is mandatory.
      SIGNATURE or SUBSCRIPTION. Includes a mark when the person cannot write.
      STATE. The State of Oregon.
      SUBCHAPTER. A division of a chapter, designated in this code by a heading
in the chapter analysis and a capitalized heading in the body of the chapter,
setting apart a group of sections related by the subject matter of the heading.
Not all chapters have SUBCHAPTERS.
      WRITTEN. Any representation of words, letters or figures, whether by
printing or otherwise.
      YEAR. A calendar year, unless otherwise expressed.
§ 10.05 RULES OF INTERPRETATION.
   The construction of all ordinances of this county shall be by the following
rules, unless the construction is plainly repugnant to the intent of the County
Board of Commissioners or of the context of the same ordinance:
   (A)   AND or OR. Either conjunction shall include the other as if written
“and/or,” if the sense requires it.
   (B)   Acts by assistants. When a statute or ordinance requires an act to be
done which, by law, an agent or deputy as well may do as the principal, the
requisition shall be satisfied by the performance of the act by an authorized
agent or deputy.
   (C)   Gender; singular and plural; tenses. Words denoting the masculine
gender shall be deemed to include the feminine and neuter genders; words in the
singular shall include the plural, and words in the plural shall include the
singular; the use of a verb in the present tense shall include the future, if
applicable.
   (D)   General term. A general term following specific enumeration of terms
is not to be limited to the class enumerated unless expressly so limited.
§ 10.06 SEVERABILITY.
   If any provision of this code as now or later amended or its application to
any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect
other provisions that can be given effect without the invalid provision or
application.
§ 10.07 REFERENCE TO OTHER SECTIONS.
   Whenever in one section reference is made to another section hereof, the
reference shall extend and apply to the section referred to as subsequently
amended, revised, recodified or renumbered unless the subject matter is changed
or materially altered by the amendment or revision.
§ 10.08 REFERENCE TO OFFICES.
   Reference to a public office or officer shall be deemed to apply to any
office, officer or employee of this county exercising the powers, duties or
functions contemplated in the provision, irrespective of any transfer of
functions or change in the official title of the functionary.
§ 10.09 ERRORS AND OMISSIONS.
   (A)   If a manifest error is discovered, consisting of the misspelling of
any words; the omission of any word or words necessary to express the intention
of the provisions affected; the use of a word or words to which no meaning can
be attached; or the use of a word or words when another word or words was
clearly intended to express such intent, the spelling shall be corrected and
such word or words supplied, omitted or substituted as will conform with the
manifest intention, and the provisions shall have the same effect as though the
correct words were contained in the text as originally published.
   (B)   No alteration shall be made or permitted if any question exists
regarding the nature or extent of such error.
§ 10.10 OFFICIAL TIME.
   The official time, as established by applicable state/federal laws, shall be
the official time within this county for the transaction of all county
business.
§ 10.11 REASONABLE TIME.
   (A)   In all cases where an ordinance requires an act to be done in a
reasonable time or requires reasonable notice to be given, REASONABLE TIME OR
NOTICE shall be deemed to mean at least 24 hours’ notice.
   (B)   The time within which an act is to be done, as herein provided, shall
be computed by excluding the first day and including the last. If the last day
be Sunday, it shall be excluded.
§ 10.12 ORDINANCES REPEALED.
   This code, from and after its effective date, shall contain all of the
provisions of a general nature pertaining to the subjects herein enumerated and
embraced. All prior ordinances pertaining to the subjects treated by this code
shall be deemed repealed from and after the effective date of this code.
§ 10.13 ORDINANCES UNAFFECTED.
   All ordinances of a temporary or special nature and all other ordinances
pertaining to subjects not embraced in this code shall remain in full force and
effect unless herein repealed expressly or by necessary implication.
§ 10.14 EFFECTIVE DATE OF ORDINANCES.
   All ordinances passed by the County Board of Commissioners shall take effect
as provided in the county charter. If there is no county charter, all
ordinances passed by the County Board of Commissioners shall take effect as
provided by the County Board of Commissioners or applicable state law.
§ 10.15 REPEAL OR MODIFICATION OF ORDINANCE.
   (A)   Whenever any ordinance or part of an ordinance shall be repealed or
modified by a subsequent ordinance, the ordinance or part of an ordinance thus
repealed or modified shall continue in force until the due publication of the
ordinance repealing or modifying it when publication is required to give effect
thereto, unless otherwise expressly provided.
   (B)   No suit, proceedings, right, fine, forfeiture or penalty instituted,
created, given, secured or accrued under any ordinance previous to its repeal
shall in any way be affected, released or discharged, but may be prosecuted,
enjoined and recovered as fully as if the ordinance had continued in force
unless it is otherwise expressly provided.
   (C)   When any ordinance repealing a former ordinance, clause or provision
shall be itself repealed, the repeal shall not be construed to revive the
former ordinance, clause or provision, unless it is expressly provided.
§ 10.16 ORDINANCES WHICH AMEND OR SUPPLEMENT CODE.
   (A)   If the County Board of Commissioners shall desire to amend any
existing chapter or section of this code, the chapter or section shall be
specifically repealed and a new chapter or section, containing the desired
amendment, substituted in its place.
   (B)   Any ordinance which is proposed to add to the existing code a new
chapter or section shall indicate, with reference to the arrangement of this
code, the proper number of such chapter or section. In addition to such
indication thereof as may appear in the text of the proposed ordinance, a
caption or title shall be shown in concise form above the ordinance.
§ 10.17 SECTION HISTORIES; STATUTORY REFERENCES.
   (A)   As histories for the code sections, the specific number and passage
date of the original ordinance and any amending ordinances are listed following
the text of the code section.
Example: (Ord. 161, passed 5-13-1960; Ord. 170, passed 1-2-1979; Ord. 185,
passed 4-1-1990)
   (B)   (1)   If a statutory cite is included in the history, this indicates
that the text of the section reads substantially the same as the statute.
Example: (O.R.S. 192.410)
      (2)   If a statutory cite is set forth as a “statutory reference”
following the text of the section, this indicates that the reader should refer
to that statute for further information.
Example:
§ 39.01 PUBLIC RECORDS AVAILABLE.
      This county shall make available to any person for inspection or copying
all public records, unless otherwise exempted by state law.
   Statutory reference:
      Inspection of public records, see O.R.S. 192.314
§ 10.18 PRESERVATION OF PENALTIES, OFFENSES, RIGHTS AND LIABILITIES.
   (A)   All offenses committed under laws in force prior to the effective date
of this code shall be prosecuted and remain punishable as provided by those
laws.
   (B)   This code does not affect any rights or liabilities accrued, penalties
incurred or proceedings begun prior to the effective date of this code. The
liabilities, proceedings and rights are continued; punishments, penalties or
forfeitures shall be enforced and imposed as if this code had not been enacted.
In particular, any agreement granting permission to utilize highway rights-of-
way, contracts entered into or franchises granted, the acceptance,
establishment or vacation of any highway and the election of corporate officers
shall remain valid in all respects, as if this code had not been enacted.
§ 10.99 GENERAL PENALTY.
   Violation of any ordinance adopted by the county, unless otherwise stated in
the ordinance itself, shall be punishable, upon conviction, by a fine of not
more than $500 for a noncontinuing offense and a fine of not more than $1,000
for a continuing offense.
(Prior Code, § 1.08.010) (Ord. MC-C-5-85, passed - -1985)

Section
   
30.01   Board of Commissioners meetings
   
30.02   Non-binding referendum votes
§ 30.01 BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS MEETINGS.
   (A)   The County Board of Commissioners shall meet to conduct business on
the first and third Wednesday of each month, beginning at 9:00 a.m.
   (B)   The public shall be notified of the location of the meetings on the
published agenda of the Board of Commissioners. The public shall be noticed as
required by the State Public Meetings Law (O.R.S. 192.610 through 192.705).
   (C)   When the regularly scheduled meeting falls on a holiday, the meeting
shall be continued until the next regularly scheduled meeting date, unless the
Board of Commissioners elects to hold a special meeting of the County Board of
Commissioners. Special meetings of the County Board of Commissioners may be
called as authorized by the State Public Meetings Law (O.R.S. 192.610 through
192.705).
   (D)   Nothing in this section prohibits the County Board of Commissioners
from changing the date, time and location of a meeting, if those changes are
allowed under the State Public Meetings Law (O.R.S. 192.610 through 192.705).
(Ord. ORD-2023-2, passed 2-8-2023)
§ 30.02 NON-BINDING REFERENDUM VOTES.
   (A)   At such times as may be directed by the Board of Commissioners, the
County Clerk shall publish notice of non-binding referendum vote to be held
upon such issue as is identified by the County Board of Commissioners in said
directive. Publication and notice shall be made in the same manner as provided
by law for any election balloting. Voting (including, but not limited to,
preparation and distribution of ballots and the counting of the same) shall
also be performed in the same manner as provided by law for a general election
vote.
   (B)   Notwithstanding any other provision herein, non-binding referendum
elections may be held.
(Ord. MC-C-4-89, passed 10-4-1989)
CHAPTER 31: COUNTY OFFICIALS
Section
   
31.01   County Auditor
§ 31.01 COUNTY AUDITOR.
   (A)   Position created; appointment. There is created the position of County
Auditor, to be filled by appointment of the County Board of Commissioners.
(Prior Code, § 2.08.010)
   (B)   Qualifications; bond. The County Auditor shall qualify as provided in
O.R.S. 210.120 within 30 days from the time of appointment. Should the County
Board of Commissioners require a bond in addition to the bond requirement under
O.R.S. 210.120, the county shall be liable for payment of the additional cost
of such bond.
(Prior Code, § 2.08.020)
   (C)   Powers and duties. The County Auditor shall perform such duties as may
be described by statute or ordinance. The County Auditor shall receive all
demands, accounts or claims against the county, together with evidence in
support thereof.
(Prior Code, § 2.08.030)
   (D)   Recordkeeping duties.
      (1)   The County Auditor shall maintain records of all claims presented,
together with the evidence and support thereof, and shall keep a record showing
at all times the financial status of the county.
      (2)   The Auditor shall keep such other records as may be required by the
County Board of Commissioners and shall keep them in the manner required by
law.
(Prior Code, § 2.08.040)
   (E)   Payment of orders. The County Treasurer shall pay or endorse “not paid
for want of funds” on all orders for payment delivered by the County Auditor
after audit and approval of the underlying claims.
(Prior Code, § 2.08.050)
    (F)   Reports to the County Board of Commissioners. The County Auditor
shall make monthly reports to the County Board of Commissioners showing the
state of the finances of the county, and the orders for payments submitted
during the month, which report shall be filed. The Auditor shall make an annual
report at the close of the fiscal year, showing the total of all claims allowed
and fiscal transactions during the preceding year. The annual report shall be
submitted within 30 days after the close of the fiscal year.
(Prior Code, § 2.08.010)
(Ord. MC-A-1-82, passed - -1982)

**** PLANNING COMMISSION ****
§ 32.001 ESTABLISHED; MEMBERS; AUTHORITY.
   There is established in the county a Planning Commission of nine members,
under the authority of state statutes.
(Prior Code, § 2.12.010) (Ord. passed 4-6-1960; Ord. MC-C-3-85, passed - -1985)
§ 32.002 ORGANIZATION AND OFFICERS.
   As soon as possible after their appointment, the members of the Planning
Commission shall organize by the election of a Chairperson and secretary, and
adopt rules for the transaction of the business of the Planning Commission.
(Prior Code, § 2.12.020) (Ord. passed 4-6-1960)
§ 32.003 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Planning Commission shall exercise the powers conferred upon it by state
law.
(Prior Code, § 2.12.030) (Ord. passed 4-6-1960; Ord. MC-C-3-85, passed - -1985)
**** PIONEER MEMORIAL HOSPITAL BOARD ****
§ 32.015 APPOINTMENT; MEMBERSHIP.
   (A)   The County Board of Commissioners shall appoint the Pioneer Memorial
Hospital Board (“PMH Board”) which shall consist of five residents of the
county.
   (B)   The original PMH Board shall be those members currently serving in
that capacity.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.010) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.016 TERM OF OFFICE.
   The term of office of each member of the PMH Board shall be five years, with
one term to expire annually on December 31. Upon the expiration of each term, a
successor shall be appointed.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.020) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.017 OFFICERS.
   The PMH Board shall select from among its members a President, a Vice
President and a secretary/treasurer.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.030) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.018 REMOVAL OF MEMBERS.
   Any member of the PMH Board may be removed for cause. In such cases, a
successor shall immediately be appointed. Failure of a member to attend three
consecutive meetings of the PMH Board, unless such absences are excused, shall
constitute cause for removal from the PMH Board.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.040) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.019 VACANCIES.
   Appointments to fill vacancies on the PMH Board shall be for the unexpired
term of the replaced member.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.050) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.020 DISSOLUTION AND REAPPOINTMENT OF BOARD.
   (A)   At such time as the County Board of Commissioners determines that the
PMH Board is unable to perform the function for which it was created, it may
dissolve the Board and appoint a new PMH Board, which may or may not contain
members from the old Board. Newly appointed members shall assume the unexpired
terms of the old Board members.
   (B)   Before the County Board of Commissioners shall dissolve the Board,
however, it shall provide 30 days’ notice of its intent to do so and shall
provide an opportunity for public hearing regarding the pending dissolution.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.060) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.021 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The PMH Board shall:
   (A)   Appoint an administrator of the hospital, with approval of the County
Board of Commissioners, who shall hold office at the pleasure of the PMH Board;
   (B)   Fix the salaries of the administrator and all other employees, within
the limits of the appropriation made therefor by the County Board of
Commissioners. Such salaries shall be compensation in full for all services
rendered by such employees or administrator;
   (C)   Exercise general management and supervisory authority pertaining to
the operation of the hospital, the hospital offices, grounds and buildings and
the employees. The Board may delegate to the administrator or other employees
this authority, as is required for the most efficient operation of the Pioneer
Memorial Hospital;
   (D)   Make such rules and regulations as it may deem necessary for the
government of the hospital and related facilities, subject to the approval of
the County Board of Commissioners;
   (E)   Maintain an effective inspection of the hospital and keep itself
informed of the affairs and management thereof;
   (F)   Conduct meetings at least once each month and at such other times as
may be necessary;
   (G)   Hold an annual meeting in January of each year;
   (H)   Keep, in a book provided for that purpose, a proper record of its
proceedings, which shall be open at all times for the inspection of its members
and to the County Board of Commissioners;
   (I)   Approve and pay all just bills and accounts, including salaries and
wages;
   (J)   Make an annual report to the County Board of Commissioners, containing
a detailed audit of the operations of the hospital during the preceding year,
with a separate budget recommendation as to future operation of the hospital
and full and detailed estimates of the appropriations required for the
maintenance of the hospital for the ensuing year;
   (K)   From time to time, furnish to the County Clerk such information as to
the affairs of the hospital as the Board may require;
   (L)   Cause to be deposited with the County Treasurer all moneys in excess
of 20% over the annual operational budget; and
   (M)   Submit monthly financial reports to the County Board of Commissioners
for their inspection.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.070) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.022 HOSPITAL ADMINISTRATOR.
   (A)   Powers and duties. The administrator of the Pioneer Memorial Hospital
shall be the chief executive officer of the hospital and shall manage it in
accordance with the directions of the PMH Board, and in accordance with rules
and regulations adopted by it. The administrator shall be responsible for the
internal affairs and discipline of the Pioneer Memorial Hospital. The
administrator may discharge from the hospital any patient who willfully or
habitually violates rules thereof.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.080)
   (B)   Bond. Before entering on the discharge of his or her duties as general
administrator, the administrator shall give a bond in such sum as the PMH Board
determines necessary to secure the faithful performance of the administrator’s
duties.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.090)
(Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.023 RATES AND CHARGES.
   The PMH Board shall fix and establish basic rates for accommodations and
services supplied to patients of the hospital. If, in the judgment of a member
or members of the hospital’s organized medical staff, care and treatment is
appropriate and is ordered for a patient, such person’s ability to pay shall
not be a consideration in denying services.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.100) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.024 FUNDING.
   The County Board of Commissioners shall levy taxes annually upon all taxable
property of the county to produce such sums as in its discretion seem adequate
to provide for the acquisition, construction, equipment, maintenance, operation
and improvement of the hospital, taking into account the revenue received from
the operation of the hospital.
(Prior Code, § 2.20.110) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
**** MORROW COUNTY HEALTH BOARD ****
§ 32.035 COMPOSITION OF BOARD.
   (A)   The County Medical Board (Board) shall consist of eight residents of
the county. Those Board members in office as of the date of this subchapter
shall remain until the expiration of their term or until resignation.
   (B)   Upon the expiration or termination of any such original term, a
successor shall be appointed by the County Board of Commissioners, and all
terms following the original terms shall be for a period of four years.
   (C)   Any member of the Board may be removed for cause. In such cases, a
successor shall immediately be appointed. Failure of a member to attend three
consecutive meetings of the Board shall constitute one cause for removal from
the Board unless such absences are excused by the Board and the reasons for the
absence and the excuse are noted in the minutes.
   (D)   At such time as the County Board of Commissioners determines that the
Board is unable to perform the function for which it was created, it may
dissolve the Board and appoint a new Board, which may or may not contain
members from the old Board; newly appointed members shall assume the unexpired
terms of the old Board members. Before the County Board of Commissioners shall
dissolve the Board, however, it shall provide 30 days’ notice of its intent to
do so and shall provide an opportunity for a public hearing regarding the
pending dissolution.
   (E)   Appointments to fill vacancies on the Board shall be for the unexpired
term of the replaced member.
   (F)   The Board shall annually select from among its members a Chairperson,
a Vice Chairperson and a secretary.
   (G)   No member shall serve consecutively in excess of two four-year terms,
together with any lesser term served as an original term pursuant to division
(B) above or as a successor filling an unexpired term.
(Ord. MC-H-2-90, passed 8-15-1990)
§ 32.036 DUTIES AND POWERS OF THE BOARD.
   (A)   The Board shall appoint an administrator or administrators with
authority as set forth in §
32.037(A) over such medical facilities or services as the Board may designate
in the appointment; such administrator(s) shall hold office at the pleasure of
the Board, and the designation of authority over particular facilities or
services may, within the sole discretion of the Board, be modified from time to
time. Alternatively, the Board may contract with a corporation or other entity
to provide management services, including services of an administrator on such
terms and conditions as the parties may agree.
   (B)   The Board shall fix the salaries of county employees subject to its
authority, within the limits of the appropriation made therefor by the County
Board of Commissioners; provided, that the Board may delegate to the
administrator(s) its authority to fix the salaries of other county employees.
Such salaries shall be compensation in full for all services rendered by said
employees.
   (C)   The Board shall have the authority to adopt a personnel policy
applicable to county employees who work at county medical facilities. When
adopted and as from time to time amended, such policies shall supersede Ord.
MC-PP-1-80, as such ordinance may from time to time be amended with respect to
such employees.
   (D)   Except during such times as such facility, premises, equipment or
furnishings may be leased pursuant to §
32.039, the MCM Board shall exercise general management and supervisory
authority pertaining to the operation of county medical facilities and
services, including, but not limited to, Pioneer Memorial Hospital, Pioneer
Memorial Clinic, the North Morrow Medical Clinic, the North Morrow Ambulance
Service, Ione First Response, Lexington First Response and Irrigon First
Response, including the offices, grounds, buildings, property and employees of
the same. The Board shall have the authority, notwithstanding any other county
ordinance or policy to the contrary, to execute all contracts within the scope
of its duties under this subchapter and within budgetary limits, including,
without limitation, settlement of threatened or pending litigation, but
excepting those contracts that involve an interest in real property or have a
term extending beyond one year, unless such contracts include a provision
allowing termination either without penalty or with a penalty to be paid out of
funds set aside from a current or past appropriation, in the event sufficient
funds are not appropriated in subsequent fiscal years. The Board may delegate
to a subcommittee of one or more of its members, or the administrator, or other
employees, so much of the authority granted hereunder as may be convenient for
the efficient operation of county medical facilities and services.
   (E)   The Board shall adopt bylaws setting forth such rules and regulations
as it may deem necessary for the government of county medical facilities and
services, subject to the approval of the County Board of Commissioners. Said
bylaws shall not contravene or contradict the provisions of this subchapter,
county policy or any applicable state, federal or local law.
   (F)   Except with respect to any facility, premises, equipment or
furnishings as may be leased pursuant to §
32.039, the Board shall maintain an effective inspection of county medical
facilities and services and keep itself informed of the affairs and management
thereof.
   (G)   The Board shall conduct meetings at least once each month and at such
other times as may be necessary.
   (H)   The Board shall make an annual report to the County Board of
Commissioners, containing a detailed audit of the operations of county medical
facilities and services during the preceding year, with a separate budget
recommendation as to future operation of county medical facilities and
services, and full and detailed estimates of the appropriations required for
the maintenance of county medical facilities and services for the ensuing year.
   (I)   The Board shall, from time to time, furnish to the County Board of
Commissioners such information as the Board may require regarding the affairs
of county medical facilities and services.
   (J)   The Board shall cause to be deposited in accounts at such financial
institutions as it may designate by resolution all monies received pursuant to
the operation of county medical facilities or services which are subject to the
authority of the Board.
   (K)   The administrator shall submit monthly financial reports to the Board
for its inspection.
   (L)   The Board shall have the authority to do all other things convenient
or necessary to operate county medical facilities or services and shall have
the authority to delegate such of its powers as it shall deem appropriate to
the administrator(s) of such facilities or services, other county employees or
other agents or independent contractors retained to provide services to county
medical facilities.
(Ord. MC-H-2-90, passed 8-15-1990)
§ 32.037 FACILITY OR SERVICE ADMINISTRATORS.
   (A)   The administrator(s) appointed pursuant to §
32.036(A) shall be the chief executive officer(s) of the medical facility(ies)
or service(s) designated in his or her appointment and shall manage them in
accordance with the rules and regulations adopted by the Board. The
administrator(s) shall be responsible for the internal affairs of such medical
facility(ies) or service(s).
   (B)   Before entering on the discharge of the duties as administrator, any
administrator appointed by the Board, shall provide a bond in such sum as the
Board determines necessary to secure the faithful performance of the
administrator’s duties. The premium for said bond shall be paid from the County
Medical Fund.
(Ord. MC-H-2-90, passed 8-15-1990)
§ 32.038 RATES AND CHARGES.
   (A)   Except at such times as any facility shall be leased under §
32.039, or when the Board shall have delegated such authority to the
administrator, the Board shall fix and establish basic rates and charges for
accommodations and services supplied to the patients of county facilities.
   (B)   If, in the judgment of a member or members of the medical staff of
county facilities, care and treatment is appropriate and is ordered for a
patient, such person’s ability to pay shall not be a consideration in providing
services.
(Ord. MC-H-2-90, passed 8-15-1990)
§ 32.039 LEASE MEDICAL FACILITIES.
   (A)   Subject to the approval of the County Board of Commissioners, the
Board shall be empowered to lease any or all medical facilities subject to its
authority, together with the land and any medical equipment and office
furniture to any person or entity, for the purpose of practicing medicine or
providing medical services.
   (B)   Any such lease shall be subject to the rules and regulations of the
Board and to any further requirements of the County Board of Commissioners.
(Ord. MC-H-2-90, passed 8-15-1990)
**** NORTH MORROW AMBULANCE SERVICE BOARD ****
§ 32.050 APPOINTMENT; MEMBERSHIP.
   The County Board of Commissioners shall appoint the North Morrow Ambulance
Service (NMAS) Board, which shall consist of five residents of North Morrow
County. The original NMAS Board shall be those members currently serving in
that capacity. In making appointments to the NMAS Board, the County Board of
Commissioners shall, to the extent that there are sufficient persons available,
maintain a Board membership which consists of four members of the Emergency
Medical Technicians Association and one non-EMTA member. Employees of the NMAS
shall not be eligible for membership, except as ex officio members.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.010) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.051 TERM OF OFFICE.
   The term of office of each member of the NMAS Board shall be three years,
with one term expiring on June 30, 1986, two terms expiring on June 30, 1983
and two terms expiring on June 30, 1984. Upon the expiration of each term, a
successor shall be appointed.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.020) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.052 OFFICERS.
   The NMAS Board shall select from among its members a President, a Vice
President and a secretary/treasurer.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.030) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.053 REMOVAL OF MEMBERS.
   Any member of the NMAS Board may be removed for cause. In such cases, a
successor shall immediately be appointed. Failure of a member to attend three
consecutive meetings of the NMAS Board, unless such absences are excused, shall
constitute cause for removal from the NMAS Board.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.040) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.054 VACANCIES.
   Appointments to fill vacancies on the NMAS Board shall be for the unexpired
term of the replaced member.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.050) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.055 DISSOLUTION AND REAPPOINTMENT OF BOARD.
   At such time as the County Board of Commissioners determines that the NMAS
Board is unable to perform the function for which it was created, it may
dissolve the Board and appoint a new NMAS Board, which may or may not contain
members from the old Board. Newly appointed members shall assume unexpired
terms of the old Board members. Before the County Board of Commissioners shall
dissolve the Board, however, it shall provide 30 days’ notice of its intent to
do so and shall provide an opportunity for public hearing regarding the pending
dissolution.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.060) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.056 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The NMAS Board shall:
   (A)   Exercise general management and supervisory authority pertaining to
operation of the North Morrow Ambulance Service;
   (B)   Adopt bylaws which, after approval by the County Board of
Commissioners, shall provide necessary rules and regulations for the government
of the North Morrow Ambulance Service;
   (C)   Maintain an effective inspection of the NMAS and keep itself informed
of the affairs and management thereof;
   (D)   Conduct regularly scheduled meetings and other meetings as may be
necessary;
   (E)   Hold an annual meeting in January of each year;
   (F)   Keep, in a book provided for that purpose, a proper record of its
proceedings, which shall be open at all times for the inspection of its members
and to the County Board of Commissioners;
   (G)   Approve and pay all just bills and accounts, including salaries and
wages, in concert with the fiscal system provided for by the County Board of
Commissioners, through the County Auditor and County Treasurer;
   (H)   Make an annual report to the County Board of Commissioners, containing
a detailed audit of the operations of the NMAS during the preceding year, with
a separate budget recommendation as to future operation of the NMAS, and full
and detailed estimates of the appropriations required for the maintenance of
the NMAS for the ensuing year;
   (I)   From time to time, furnish to the County Board of Commissioners such
information as to the affairs of the NMAS as the Board may require; and
   (J)   Submit monthly financial reports to the County Board of Commissioners
for its inspection.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.070) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
§ 32.057 SERVICE RATES AND CHARGES.
   The NMAS Board shall fix and establish rates and charges associated with the
NMAS. If, in the judgment of a member of the NMAS staff, care and treatment or
services are necessary for a patient, such person’s inability to pay shall not
be a consideration in denying services.
(Prior Code, § 2.28.080) (Ord. MC-H-1-83, passed - -1983)
**** INTERIM BOARD OF DIRECTORS ****
§ 32.070 TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Special District
Interim Board of Directors Ordinance.”
(Ord. MC-C-3-95, passed 3-8-1995)
§ 32.071 APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM BOARD OF DIRECTORS.
   Whenever a special district is proposed to be formed in the county, the
County Board of Commissioners may appoint an Interim Board of Directors to act
by and on behalf of the proposed district prior to regular election of a Board
of Directors; provided, that:
   (A)   The district is proposed to be formed by order of the County Board of
Commissioners, without a tax base;
   (B)   The formation process has proceeded to the point of establishment of
boundaries and declaration by the County Board of Commissioners of its
intention to enter an order creating the district; and
   (C)   The County Board of Commissioners finds that an emergency exists, in
that the lack of existence of an authorized board will result in failure to
meet auxiliary statutory deadlines, such as certification of ballot titles, and
that such failure will thwart the purpose or purposes for which the district is
proposed to be formed, or will result in significant undue hardship for the
county residents who will benefit from formation of the district.
(Ord. MC-C-3-95, passed 3-8-1995)
§ 32.072 LIMITATIONS.
   The authority of any Interim Board appointed by the County Board of
Commissioners shall be limited solely to the performance of those actions
necessary to comply with statutory deadlines for elections or Department of
Revenue requirements. Such Interim Board may certify ballot titles, send
appropriate maps to the Department of Revenue, or take other similar action,
however, such Interim Board shall not be authorized to perform any action which
interferes with the right of the people of the county to vote on the ultimate
issues of district formation or tax levy approval.
(Ord. MC-C-3-95, passed 3-8-1995)
§ 32.073 TIME AND MANNER OF APPOINTMENT.
   If it appears to the County Board of Commissioners that a district
undergoing the formation process will be deprived of its primary purpose by
failure to comply with auxiliary statutory deadlines because it lacks a board
to act for it during the formation process, the County Board of Commissioners
may appoint, by resolution, an Interim Board of Directors. There shall be the
same number of members appointed to the Interim Board as are proposed for the
district undergoing formation. In the event that the district is not formed,
the Interim Board shall immediately dissolve and shall have no further
authority of any kind to act with regard to matters involving the failed
district.
(Ord. MC-C-3-95, passed 3-8-1995)

Section

   Complete personnel rules are on file with Ord. MC-PP-1-80 in the office of

§ 34.01 TITLE.
   The title of this chapter shall be “The Personnel Ordinance of Morrow
County.”
(Prior Code, § 2.36.010) (Ord. MC-PP-1-80, passed - -1980)
§ 34.02 PURPOSE.
   The ordinance codified in this chapter was adopted to establish an equitable
and uniform procedure for dealing with personnel matters; to attract to county
service and to retain the best and most competent persons available; to assure
that appointments and promotions of employees will be based on merit and
fitness; and to provide a reasonable degree of job security for qualified
employees.
(Prior Code, § 2.36.020) (Ord. MC-PP-1-80, passed - -1980)
§ 34.03 ADOPTION AND AMENDMENT.
   Personnel rules shall be adopted and amended by resolution of the County
Board of Commissioners. The rules shall provide means to recruit, select,
develop and maintain an effective and responsive work force and shall include
policies and procedures for employee hiring and advancement, training and
career development, job classification, salary administration, retirement,
fringe benefits, discipline, dismissal and other related activities. All
appointments and promotions shall be made in accordance with the personnel
rules, without regard to sex, race, color, age, religion or political
affiliation and, furthermore, shall be based on merit and fitness.
(Prior Code, § 2.36.030) (Ord. MC-PP-1-80, passed - -1980)
§ 34.04 ADMINISTRATION.
   The Board shall be responsible for:
   (A)   Administering all the provisions of this chapter and of the personnel
rules not specifically reserved to the department heads; and
   (B)   Preparing (or causing to be prepared) of personnel rules and revisions
and amendments to such rules.
(Prior Code, § 2.36.040) (Ord. MC-PP-1-80, passed - -1980)
§ 34.05 APPLICABILITY.
   For negotiated labor agreements, any section, division, sentence, clause or
phrase of these rules that is found to be inconsistent with the expressed terms
of a properly negotiated and ratified collective bargaining agreement between
the county and a duly certified bargaining representative, and any other
provision contained herein, the application of which would be inappropriate
either because of alternate provisions contained in such a collectively
bargained agreement, or arising out of the county’s obligation to bargain over
such items, shall not apply to those employees subject to such collectively
bargained agreement.
(Prior Code, § 2.36.050) (Ord. MC-PP-1-80, passed - -1980)
§ 34.06 EQUAL OPPORTUNITY AND AFFIRMATIVE ACTION POLICY.
   (A)   It is the policy of the county to provide equal employment opportunity
to all persons.
   (B)   All county recruitment, hiring, training, promoting and transferring
shall be done without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex,
political affiliation, age or physical or mental handicaps not constituting
bona fide occupation qualifications, and all personnel policies, procedures and
practices shall be administered accordingly.
   (C)   The county recognizes its moral and legal responsibility to provide
equal employment opportunity, to take affirmative and direct action at all
levels of county government, regarding job classification, salaries, training,
fringe benefits and other personnel policies, and to improve employment and
career opportunities for minority group persons and women according to
affirmative action principles.
   (D)   The county will advertise any job openings that exist in the Personnel
Department at least once in the official county newspaper. Applicants will be
considered on the basis of merit and in accordance with the policies as
outlined above.
(Prior Code, § 2.36.060) (Ord. MC-PP-1-80, passed - -1980)
