§ 51.21 FRANCHISING OF SOLID WASTE COLLECTION.
   No person shall solicit for service customers or provide solid waste
collection service for compensation in the county without first acquiring a
franchise as required by this subchapter unless specifically exempted as listed
in this section. This franchise requirement does not apply within the limits of
an incorporated city, except as may be provided through an agreement between
the city and the county.
   (A)   Exemptions to requirement for solid waste collection franchise. The
following persons or practices are exempt from the requirements of this
section:
      (1)   A private charitable organization which regularly engages in the
collection and reuse of repairable or cleanable discards, such as the Salvation
Army, St. Vincent DePaul, Goodwill and similar organizations;
      (2)   A religious, charitable, benevolent or fraternal organization,
which is not organized for solid waste management purposes, and which is using
the activity for fund raising, such as scouts and churches, and which collects,
reuses or recycles totally source separated materials or operates a collection
center for totally source separated materials;
      (3)   The collection, transportation or redemption of returnable beverage
containers under the “Bottle Bill” (O.R.S. Chapter 459A);
      (4)   A producer who transports and disposes of waste created as an
incidental part of the regular operation of a licensed business, such as an
auto wrecking business, a janitorial service, a gardening or landscaping
service and a septic tank pumping or sludge collection or disposal service;
      (5)   A person who deals in the practice or business of totally source
separated solid wastes and selling these materials for fair market value and
when the activity has been licensed under this subchapter with a recycling
license under §
51.22; and
      (6)   A self-hauler, as defined in §
51.16, hauling solid waste and/or recyclables to a permitted solid waste
disposal site.
   (B)   Application for a collection franchise.
      (1)   Application for a collection franchise shall be made on forms
provided by the Administrator. In addition to information required on the
forms, the Administrator may require the filing of any additional information
deemed necessary to ensure compliance with this subchapter. The forms shall
provide for the application for a new collection franchise, a transfer or an
expansion of the collection area.
      (2)   An applicant for a collection franchise or for a collection
franchise transfer shall demonstrate the following to the satisfaction of the
Board:
         (a)   The need for the collection service in the area applied for;
         (b)   Has a majority of the service accounts in the service area for
which they have applied, as evidenced by a list of customers served;
         (c)   The applicant has available collection vehicles, equipment,
land, facilities, personnel and sufficient financial resources to provide the
proposed service and to meet the standards established by O.R.S. Chapter 459
and applicable administrative rules. If the applicant proposes to serve an area
which is wholly or in part under franchise to another person/organization, or
to replace such person/organization upon expiration of the existing franchise,
the applicant shall have available on the beginning date of the proposed
franchise term collection vehicles, containers and other equipment equal to
that presently used in servicing the area;
         (d)   The applicant has sufficient experience to ensure compliance
with this subchapter. If the applicant does not have sufficient experience to
the satisfaction of the Board, the Board may require the applicant to submit a
corporate surety bond, issued by a person or company authorized to do business
in the state, in the amount of not less than $20,000, guaranteeing full and
faithful performance by the applicant of the duties and obligations of a
franchisee under the provisions of this subchapter and applicable federal,
state and local laws and rules or regulations and holding the county harmless
from liability;
         (e)   The applicant shall submit a certification acceptable to the
County Board of Commissioners of public liability insurance with a 30-day
notice of cancellation clause, covering the business’s operations and including
coverage of each vehicle operated by the applicant. The insurance coverage
shall be in the amounts equal to, or over the amounts established as the
minimum requirements by the State Tort Claims Act, being O.R.S. 30.260 et seq.,
now in force or as modified by future legislative action. The insurance shall
indemnify and hold the county harmless against any liability or damage to
persons or property arising from the franchisee’s business operation; and
         (f)   When requesting a transfer of franchise, the applicant must
submit, as part of the application, a letter from the current franchisee
requesting the transfer.
   (C)   Existing collection providers. Persons providing collection service on
the effective date of this subchapter, whether or not that service has been
already provided pursuant to a franchise or order, and who are not exempt under
this subchapter shall file an application for an appropriate franchise together
with any required information within 60 days after the effective date of this
subchapter. Upon filing the application, such person shall continue to provide
existing service until a final determination on the application is made by the
County Board of Commissioners or a circuit court on appeal.
   (D)   Application review.
      (1)   Applications shall be reviewed by the Administrator who shall make
such investigation as the Administrator deems appropriate and who may request
assistance of other persons as necessary.
      (2)   Upon receipt of an application, the Administrator shall give notice
to the holder of or applicant of another franchise for any part of the service
area under consideration, or whose existing or proposed service area would
likely be affected by the franchise application under consideration.
      (3)   Unless the time is extended by the Board for good cause, the
Administrator shall make a recommendation on the franchise to the Board within
30 days after the application and any required supplemental information have
been received.
      (4)   The Board:
         (a)   May require additional investigation to be made or information
to be submitted;
         (b)   May, after providing written notice to interested persons, call
an informational public hearing to allow interested persons to testify orally
or in writing;
         (c)   Shall, upon the basis of the application and any evidence or
testimony submitted, and the Administrator’s recommendation, make a finding on
the qualifications of the applicant and also on whether additional area should
be included; additional services should be provided; additional equipment,
facilities, land or personnel should be provided; and whether additional
conditions should be imposed; and
         (d)   Shall, upon the basis of its findings, grant, deny, modify or
attach appropriate conditions to the application within 30 days from the date
of receipt of the recommendation from the Administrator.
      (5)   Upon receipt of the order granting the franchise, the applicant
shall enter into a written franchise agreement with the county which requires
compliance with this subchapter, any applicable provisions of O.R.S. Chapter
459 and any rules promulgated thereunder. The agreement shall provide for the
franchisee or the county to, upon mutual agreement, negotiate amendments or
modifications of the agreement.
      (6)   If the Board makes a final order rejecting all or part of the
application for a franchise, the applicant may not submit another application
containing all or a portion of the same service area for a period of six months
unless this provision is waived by the Board upon a finding that the public
interest requires reconsideration within a shorter period of time.
   (E)   Responsibilities of franchisees.
      (1)   Service. Franchisees shall furnish adequate and reliable service as
authorized and required by the franchise and this subchapter, O.R.S. Chapters
459 and 459A and all other applicable laws, rules or regulations and at rates
established by the Board.
      (2)   Recycling. The franchisee shall work with the county to help
implement and meet the state reuse and recycling requirements as outlined in
the franchise agreement.
      (3)   Discontinuation of service. Except as provided in division (E)(6)
below, no franchisee shall voluntarily discontinue service to any of their
service area until the franchisee has:
         (a)   Given 90-day written notice to affected customers in the service
area;
         (b)   Given 90-day written notice to the Administrator; and
         (c)   Obtained approval of the Board.
      (4)   Complaints and records.
         (a)   The franchisee shall respond in a timely manner to any written
complaints regarding service.
         (b)   The franchisee shall keep accurate books and records which shall
be available during regular business hours for inspection and review by a
qualified person designated by the Administrator. Records shall be generated
and maintained according to general accounting practices.
      (5)   Reporting. The franchisee shall file, at a minimum, an annual
franchise report to the County Board of Commissioners for the preceding year as
stipulated in the franchise agreement. Additionally, the franchisee shall
submit a recycling report to the Administrator.
      (6)   Exceptions. This subchapter shall not apply to termination of
collection service due to:
         (a)   Damage, destruction or failure of equipment due to an act of
God;
         (b)   Adverse weather which makes service impossible;
         (c)   Change, restriction or termination of service when required by
any public agency, public body or court having jurisdiction;
         (d)   Customer refusal to pay for service in accordance with
franchisee’s established rates;
         (e)   Transfer of franchises pursuant to this subchapter;
         (f)   A finding by the Administrator that service at the particular
location would jeopardize the safety of the driver of a collection vehicle or
of the motoring public, that the customer has not provided reasonable access to
the pickup point for the solid waste containers or recyclable materials without
hazard or risk to the person providing service, or that weather conditions
prevent service to the particular customer;
         (g)   Noncompliance with any rule or regulation as outlined in the
franchise; and
         (h)   Road closures.
   (F)   Rate standards.
      (1)   Upon recommendation by the SWAC, the County Board of Commissioners
shall be responsible for the determination of rates or the establishment of
rates, the adjustment of existing rates and the adjustment of existing rate
differentials by zone. This determination shall be based upon information
submitted by the franchisee and shall be determined at a public hearing.
      (2)   When a franchisee wishes to adjust existing rates, a written
request, with justification, shall be made to the Administrator. Before any
rate is adjusted, the Administrator shall conduct an investigation and make a
recommendation to the Solid Waste Advisory Committee (SWAC) at a regularly
scheduled SWAC meeting, who will then make a recommendation to the County Board
of Commissioners. The County Board of Commissioners shall consider the matter
at a regularly scheduled public hearing. The County Board of Commissioners
shall then issue an order, setting forth its findings and the appropriate rates
and their effective date.
      (3)   In consideration of rate adjustment, the SWAC and County Board of
Commissioners shall give consideration to, but not be limited to, the
following:
         (a)   Current and projected revenues;
         (b)   Current and projected operating expenses;
         (c)   Acquisition and replacement of equipment;
         (d)   Professional and consultant services;
         (e)   Construction and maintenance costs;
         (f)   Research, training and development;
         (g)   Special services;
         (h)   Recycling costs;
         (i)   Reasonable operating margin; and
         (j)   Other matters as deemed relevant by the Board.
      (4)   Where no rate has been established for a particular type of
service, the County Board of Commissioners may establish an interim rate,
pursuant to the factors listed above, and included therein shall be a time
limit on the interim rate not to exceed 60 days until a final determination is
made by the County Board of Commissioners.
    (G)   Renewal of franchise. The franchise shall begin at the adoption of
the order and shall be considered as a continuing five-year franchise. That is,
beginning January 1 of each year, the franchise will be considered renewed for
an additional five-year term, unless at least 90 days prior to January 1 of any
year either party shall notify the other party in writing of intent to
terminate further renewals of this franchise. The Board may later reinstate
continuing renewals upon mutual agreement with the franchisee. Nothing in this
section restricts the Board from suspending, modifying or revoking the
franchise for cause as outlined in succeeding sections of this subchapter.
   (H)   Interruption of service. Whenever the Board finds that a franchisee’s
interruption of service could result in creation of a health hazard or a public
or private nuisance, the Board shall have the right to, in an emergency order,
issue a franchise to a qualified solid waste collector to provide service so
long as the immediate danger to the public health, or public or private
nuisance continues.
   (I)   Enforcement and corrective action. The following actions may be taken.
      (1)   Investigation. The Administrator, upon reasonable cause, may make
an investigation to determine if there has been a violation of this subchapter
by the franchisee.
      (2)   Notice of violation. If, in the judgment of the Administrator,
based upon his or her investigation, there is sufficient evidence to conclude
there has been a violation, the Administrator shall notify the franchisee, in
writing, of the violation and require the franchisee to take steps to correct
the violation and to follow the requirements set forth in the notice. The
Administrator shall send a copy of the notice to the Board.
      (3)   Response. The franchisee shall provide a written response to the
notice within ten calendar days of receipt. The response shall indicate whether
the franchisee agrees that there has been a violation and whether, when and how
corrective action will be taken. If it appears that the franchisee is unable to
or refuses to correct the violation, the Administrator shall make a
recommendation to the Board concerning appropriate action. The Administrator
may recommend that the franchise be suspended, modified or revoked or that it
not be renewed, or that any conditions the Administrator deems appropriate be
imposed.
   (J)   Suspension, modification, revocation or refusal to renew franchise.
Upon recommendation of the Administrator or on the Board’s own motion, the
Board may suspend, modify, revoke or refuse to renew a franchise upon a finding
that the franchisee has:
      (1)   Willfully violated this subchapter or O.R.S. Chapter 459, the
franchise or rules or regulations promulgated thereunder;
      (2)   Made a material misrepresentation in any written documents required
to be submitted by the franchisee;
      (3)   Willfully refused to provide service required by this subchapter or
the franchise, or to take any corrective action required under this subchapter
after written notification and a reasonable opportunity to do so; or
      (4)   Misrepresented the gross receipts from the franchise service area
if such reports are required to be submitted by this subchapter or by order of
the Board.
   (K)   Effective date; emergency order. If the Board, by order, suspends,
modifies, revokes or refuses to renew a franchise, the action shall not become
effective until 30 days after the date of the order unless the Board finds that
the order should take effect earlier to prevent a serious and immediate danger
to the public health or a public nuisance. The Board may, in an emergency
order, issue a franchise to a qualified solid waste collector to provide
service so long as the immediate danger to the public health or public nuisance
continues.
   (L)   Public hearing. The affected franchisee may request a public hearing
before the Board by filing a written request for such hearing with the Board
within 30 days after the date of the order. Upon filing the request, the Board
shall set a time and place for a public hearing. Unless the Board finds it
necessary to prevent a serious and immediate danger to the public health or a
public nuisance, the Board’s action shall not take effect until after the
public hearing and final order. The franchisee, other interested persons,
affected public agencies or bodies may submit oral or written evidence to the
Board relevant to the Board’s order.
   (M)   Final order. The Board shall, following the public hearing and within
30 days thereafter, affirm, amend or rescind its prior order based upon the
evidence contained in the record of the public hearing. The Board shall make
written findings of fact based upon such evidence. Subject to circuit court
review, pursuant to O.R.S. 34.010 et seq., the determination of the County
Board of Commissioners shall be final.
(Ord. MC-03-06, passed 4-19-2006)
§ 51.22 LICENSING FOR RECYCLING.
   No person shall collect solid waste or source separated recyclable material
with the intent to recycle as a for-profit business within the unincorporated
county without first obtaining a recycling license under this subchapter. No
license shall be issued to recyclers who intend to charge a fee for receiving
materials meant to be recycled.
   (A)   Exemptions. The county will exempt the following persons from the
recycling license requirement so long as that person reports recycled material
toward meeting the state mandated recycling goals when recycling reporting is
applicable to a particular activity:
      (1)   A persons who sells their own source separated recyclable material
generated from their residence or business, excluding those source separated
recyclable materials generated by their tenant(s);
      (2)   Persons who are authorized by franchise or under this subchapter to
collect recyclables;
      (3)   Persons who transport recyclable materials from outside the county
or through the county;
      (4)   Persons who collect, dispose of or recycle, rendered animal
products, forest products or industrial residues (not to include principal
recyclable materials as determined by the Department of Environmental Quality)
or materials used for productive purposes in agricultural operations;
      (5)   Persons licensed by the state and engaged in conducting business as
an auto wrecker or dismantler;
      (6)   Any retail outlet that collects waste oil from the public at no
fee;
      (7)   A private charitable organization which regularly engages in the
collection and reuse of repairable or cleanable discards, such as the Salvation
Army, St. Vincent DePaul, Goodwill and similar organizations;
      (8)   A religious, charitable, benevolent or fraternal organization,
which is not organized for solid waste management purposes, and which is using
the activity for fund raising, such as scouts and churches, and which collects,
reuses or recycles totally source separate materials or operates a collection
center for totally source separated materials; and
      (9)   The collection, transportation or redemption of returnable beverage
containers under the “Bottle Bill” (O.R.S. Chapter 459A).
   (B)   Application. Application for a recycling license shall be made on
forms provided by the Administrator for County Board of Commissioners approval.
In addition to information required on the forms, the Administrator may require
the filing of any additional information deemed necessary to ensure compliance
with this subchapter.
   (C)   Applicant requirements. Each applicant shall demonstrate to the
satisfaction of the County Board of Commissioners that:
      (1)   The applicant has obtained land use approval for the recycling site
or facility. The land use approval shall utilize the County Zoning Ordinance
and applicable criteria;
      (2)   The applicant has the knowledge, ability and training necessary to
safely manage hazardous materials and emergency response, if applicable;
      (3)   The applicant is able to document end-use markets or provide
evidence that the recyclable material can and will be periodically moved off
the facility property to markets; and
      (4)   The applicant has appropriate financial assurance to ensure proper
closing and/or cleanup of the facility consistent with state environmental
requirements.
   (D)   License requirements.
      (1)   Each license shall be dated as of the first day of the month in
which it is issued or the month when it was required to have been obtained, and
it shall expire one year from that date. The license will be considered
automatically renewed each year unless at least 60 days prior to the normal
expiration date of the license either party shall notify the other party in
writing of intent to terminate further renewals of this license.
      (2)   The recycling license will be the controlling document wherein the
County Board of Commissioners specifies the terms and conditions and financial
assurances necessary for the recycling activity. The license shall hold the
condition that the licensee not place a charge on receiving materials meant to
be recycled.
   (E)   Financial assurance.
      (1)   The amount of financial assurance required by the County Board of
Commissioners shall be negotiated on a case-by-case basis to be calculated
based on the following considerations:
         (a)   The potential cost of removal and disposal or sale of materials
in the case of the premises being abandoned or the operator becoming insolvent;
         (b)   Site cleanup as a result of gradual contamination; and
         (c)   Cleanup of sudden and accidental events.
      (2)   The assurance may be in the form of insurance, letter of credit,
performance or surety bond, cashier’s check or a certificate of deposit drawn
on an established state bank. The county may set up a fund to be contributed to
by recycling licensees from which recycling mitigation expenses incurred by the
above events could be paid for.
   (F)   Recordkeeping.
      (1)   Each person required to be licensed under this subchapter shall
furnish to the Administrator, on such forms as the licensee shall provide,
information including the manner in which recyclables are being collected or
received and the amounts of such materials received. Such report shall be
furnished at times designated by the Administrator but at least on an annual
basis. The report may coincide with reporting requirements of the Department of
Environmental Quality.
      (2)   Failure to furnish such information as required by the
Administrator shall be grounds for refusal to issue another recycling license
upon expiration of the current license period.
(Ord. MC-03-06, passed 4-19-2006)
§ 51.23 LICENSING OF SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL.
   In order to provide for the protection and preservation of land uses which
might be adversely impacted by solid waste disposal and to ensure that solid
waste disposal sites and facilities, including composting facilities, will not
constitute nuisances to other land uses, no solid waste disposal site shall be
established, maintained, substantially altered, expanded or improved until the
person operating such site has obtained an State Department of Environmental
Quality permit, land use approval and a solid waste contract/agreement from the
county. This requirement does not apply within the limits of an incorporated
city, except as may be provided through an agreement between the city and the
county.
   (A)   Conditions for exemptions to requirement for solid waste disposal
license. All solid waste disposal sites listed hereunder may be exempted from
approval as required by this subchapter, after administrative review prior to
an allowance as an exception:
      (1)   Any disposal site not required to have an State Department of
Environmental Quality or State Department of Agriculture permit;
      (2)   A landfill which is used by the owner or person in control of the
premises to dispose of clean fill materials;
      (3)   A portion of land or a facility specifically possessing a waste
water discharge permit pursuant to O.R.S. Chapter 468 and in compliance with
all State Environmental Quality Commission regulations on solid waste
management;
      (4)   Land on which solid wastes are used, at agronomic rates, for
fertilizer or for other productive purposes in agricultural operations, not
including composting facilities; and
      (5)   County owned and operated facilities.
   (B)   Application. Application for a disposal site license shall be made on
forms provided by the Administrator. In addition to information required on the
forms, the Administrator may require the filing of any additional information
it deems necessary to ensure compliance with this subchapter. The forms shall
provide for the application for a new disposal license or a transfer of
license.
   (C)   Requirements.
      (1)   An applicant for a disposal site license shall submit a valid
Department of Environmental Quality permit for the site or facility, or a
duplicate of the information submitted to the Department of Environmental
Quality for a disposal site under O.R.S. Chapter 459 and applicable rules.
      (2)   An applicant shall seek and obtain a land use permit for the
disposal site or facility. The land use permit shall utilize the County Zoning
Ordinance and applicable criteria.
      (3)   Each applicant for a disposal site license shall supply a plan for
rehabilitation and use of the disposal site after disposal has been terminated,
and such use shall be a use permitted within the land use zone in which such
land is located.
      (4)   The applicant shall have available land, equipment, management,
facilities and personnel to meet the standards established by O.R.S. Chapter
459 and applicable rules, and have insurance equal to that required for a
collection franchise, as described in §
51.21.
      (5)   The applicant for a disposal site license shall demonstrate to the
satisfaction of the Board that the applicant will provide a place for the
deposit of recyclable material, if applicable.
      (6)   The applicant shall have sufficient experience to ensure compliance
with O.R.S. Chapter 459 and this subchapter. If the applicant does not have
sufficient experience, the Board may either deny the application or require the
applicant to submit a corporate surety bond which guarantees full and faithful
performance by the applicant of the duties and obligations of a license holder
under this subchapter and guarantees compliance with all applicable laws, and
which holds the county harmless.
      (7)   If the application is for a transfer of a disposal site contract,
the applicant must submit, as part of the application, a letter from the
current holder requesting the transfer.
   (D)   Existing disposal site license holders. Persons holding valid
Department of Environmental Quality disposal site or valid State Department of
Agriculture permits for disposal sites in the county on the effective date of
this subchapter, and who are without a county contract or order for a disposal
site, and who have not been exempted under this subchapter, shall file an
application for a disposal site license within 60 days after the effective date
of this subchapter. Upon filing the application, such person shall continue to
provide existing service until a final determination on the application is made
by the County Board of Commissioners.
   (E)   Application review.
      (1)   Applications shall be reviewed by the Administrator, which shall
make such investigation as he or she deems appropriate. The Administrator shall
give written notice of any application to affected license holders and
adjoining property owners. Upon the basis of the disposal site application,
evidence submitted and results of any investigation, the Administrator shall
make a finding and recommendation on the qualifications of the applicant,
whether additional service, land, equipment or facilities should be provided
and what conditions of service should be imposed, including whether the site
should be opened to the public and under what conditions, whether or not
certain types of wastes, solid wastes or hazardous wastes should be excluded
from the site or what types of wastes should be required to be accepted at the
site and whether the site complies with all rules and regulations adopted
pursuant to this subchapter and O.R.S. Chapter 459.
      (2)   Unless the time is extended by the Board for good cause, the
Administrator shall make a recommendation on the disposal site application to
the Board within 30 days after the application and any required supplemental
information have been received.
      (3)   The Board shall conduct a public hearing to consider an application
within 30 days of the Administrator’s recommendation. Notice shall be served on
the applicant, adjoining property owners and any affected right holder, and
shall be published once in the newspapers generally circulated within the
county, not more than 20 or fewer than seven days, preceding the hearing. The
County Board of Commissioners:
         (a)   May require additional investigation to be made or information
to be submitted;
         (b)   Shall, upon the basis of the application, any evidence or
testimony submitted, and the Administrator’s recommendation, make a finding on
the qualifications of the applicant on whether additional area should be
included; additional services should be provided; additional equipment,
facilities, land or personnel should be provided; and whether conditions should
be imposed on disposal or recycling; and
         (c)   Shall, upon the basis of its findings, grant, deny, modify or
attach appropriate conditions deemed necessary to carry out the purposes and
policy of this subchapter to the applicant within 30 days from the date of
receipt of the recommendation from the Administrator. The determination of the
Board after conclusion of the public hearing shall be final. If the Board’s
order rejects all or part of the application, the applicant may not submit
another application for the same disposal site for a period of six months,
unless the Board finds that the public interest requires reconsideration within
a shorter period of time.
      (4)   After the applicant has received an order granting a license for
the solid waste disposal site, the applicant shall enter into a written
contract and agreement with the county which requires compliance with this
subchapter and any applicable provisions of O.R.S. Chapters 459 and 459A. The
agreement will be the controlling document wherein the County Board of
Commissioners and the applicant agree upon the license review periods, (if
any), terms and conditions, fees, additional fees, closure fees and dedicated
fees which are required as a condition of the license for a disposal site.
   (F)   Responsibilities of license holders.
      (1)   Holders shall furnish all service authorized and required by the
license, the Department of Environmental Quality, this subchapter and the
agreement, at rates established by the Board for the term of the license.
      (2)   A holder shall, where applicable, provide, maintain and use
adequate equipment to handle and dispose of or resource recover solid waste;
handle collected solid wastes in a good and capable manner; transport all
liquids in a water-tight, drip-proof container; and provide equipment that
meets all applicable laws, codes, regulations and standards.
      (3)   A disposal site license holder shall not discontinue required
service without 90 days’ written notice to the Board and to any collection
franchise or license holders having use of the site. Board approval shall be
obtained before such discontinuance unless the discontinuance is due to the
decision of administrative, legislative and judicial agencies having
jurisdiction.
      (4)   A holder shall make the fee payments as provided promptly as they
become due.
      (5)   The holder of a solid waste disposal license shall maintain a
current and valid permit from the State Department of Environmental Quality or
the State Department of Agriculture.
   (G)   Transfer of pledge for a disposal license.
      (1)   A license shall not be sold, transferred or assigned to another
person without prior written approval of the Board which shall not be
unreasonably withheld.
      (2)   A person desiring a license transfer shall submit an application to
the Administrator on forms provided by the Administrator. The Administrator
shall review the application and forward a recommendation to the County Board
of Commissioners. The Board shall then hold a public hearing and vote to
approve or deny the request.
      (3)   The term of the transferred license shall continue for the same
period as the original license.
(Ord. MC-03-06, passed 4-19-2006)
§ 51.24 FEES.
   Fees and revenue collected pursuant to this subchapter shall be expended for
solid waste management related activities. These fees and revenues shall
include, but not be limited to, revenue generated from any licensed solid waste
site or facility such as the franchised solid waste collectors, recycling
licensees, transfer facilities, landfills and other disposal sites. The budget
from the monies shall include and establish amounts to be reserved for solid
waste management activities, including, but not limited to: solid waste
education; protecting the environment; providing financial stability; meeting
contractual obligations; providing for future solid waste facilities; and
addressing changes in legal requirements. The budget recommendations prepared
by the Administrator shall be reviewed and be subject to approval through the
county’s annual budget process pursuant to the State Local Budget Law, being
O.R.S. 294.305 et seq., and applicable county policies.
   (A)   Application fees. An application required by this subchapter shall be
accompanied by a filing fee in the amount as set forth by the County Board of
Commissioners in the County Fee Ordinance. Said fees may be amended by County
Board of Commissioners order after conducting a hearing thereon.
      (1)   All fees shall be due and payable at the time the application or
appeal is submitted. No application or appeal shall be accepted without the
proper fee being paid.
      (2)   If it is determined by the Administrator at the time of application
or at any time during the application process, that staff time and departmental
costs to process a specific application will be significantly greater than that
of other typical applications, the Administrator may require an applicant to
enter into a memorandum of agreement with the county which would establish a
fee based upon actual staff time and departmental costs. If an applicant
refuses to enter into a memorandum of agreement or there is failure to
negotiate an acceptable fee, the applicant may appeal the Administrator’s
decision to the County Board of Commissioners for resolution. If the applicant
and the county fail to reach an agreement, the application will not be
processed.
   (B)   Collection franchise fees. Collection franchise fees shall be paid to
the county on a regular basis as required by the franchise agreement,
accompanied by a sworn and verified statement as to the gross receipts for the
previous calendar year. The Board may conduct an audit of the franchisee’s
books to determine the accuracy of the franchisee’s statement of gross
receipts.
   (C)   Recycling license fees. A recycling license holder shall pay an annual
fee based on the County Fee Ordinance. The Board may waive this fee in order to
promote reuse or recycling.
   (D)   Disposal site license fees. A disposal site license holder shall pay
regular fees based on tippage or other individual requirements of each license,
as ordered by the Board and stipulated in the agreement. Fees the County Board
of Commissioners may consider include, but are not limited to, dedicated road
fees, tippage fees or surcharges.
   (E)   Finley Buttes Regional Landfill Closure Fund. The Closure Fund,
established in § 10 of the agreement between the county and Tidewater Barge
Lines and guaranteed under the transfer of Finley Buttes Landfill Company to
Waste Connections, Inc. allows, under § 10.5 of said agreement, that when the
Closure Fund exceeds $1,000,000, the excess funds shall be utilized
exclusively, in accordance with DEQ administrative rules, to reduce solid waste
disposal rates of persons within the county or to enhance solid waste disposal
facilities within the county.
   (F)   Transfer station fees.
      (1)   The county operated transfer stations shall charge a fee for the
deposit of solid waste at a county transfer station based on the County Fee
Ordinance. Additionally, the caretakers of the transfer station shall impose a
penalty, also based on the County Fee Ordinance, upon each load or deposit
which is brought to the transfer station and which is not covered and secured
so as to prevent leakage, spillage or loss during transport.
      (2)   All moneys collected at a county operated transfer station shall be
deposited to the appropriate solid waste transfer station line items in the
County General Fund.
(Ord. MC-03-06, passed 4-19-2006)
§ 51.25 OVERSIGHT AND ENFORCEMENT.
   The Administrator, under the supervision of the County Board of
Commissioners, shall be responsible for the oversight and enforcement of the
County Solid Waste Management Ordinance.
   (A)   Parties bound. The term of a collection franchise, recycling or
disposal license shall be binding upon the franchisee or licensee, its heirs,
executors, administrators, successors and assigns.
   (B)   Acceptance.
      (1)   Any franchise granted under this subchapter shall be inoperative
unless the franchisee files with the county the executed franchise agreement
within 60 days of the Board approval of the franchise.
      (2)   The franchise agreement shall constitute an irrevocable contract
between the county and the franchisee, subject to termination only as provided
under this subchapter or in the franchise agreement.
   (C)   Severability and appeals.
      (1)   If any section, division, sentence, clause or portion of this
subchapter is for any reason held invalid or declared unconstitutional by any
court of competent jurisdiction, that portion shall be deemed a separate,
distinct and independent provision, and the holding shall not affect the
constitutionality of the remaining portion hereof.
      (2)   Any appeal of an action by the County Board of Commissioners shall
be made pursuant to O.R.S. 34.010 through 34.100, writs of review and shall be
filed with the County Circuit Court.
   (D)   Enforcement.
      (1)   The owner, title holder, contract seller or contract buyer of the
land upon which a violation is occurring is equally responsible for the
violation of this subchapter, as is the possessor of the land, user of the land
or the person which is taking the action, conduct or omission which constitutes
a violation of this subchapter.
      (2)   A franchise or license holder shall at all times be subject to
applicable laws of the state. A violation of state law, if found by the Board
to be substantial and material to the policy of this subchapter, may be deemed
by the Board to be a breach of the franchise or license.
      (3)   If a holder breaches any of the terms or payments required under
the terms of this subchapter and such default continues for a period of ten
calendar days after receipt of written notification sent by certified mail by
the Administrator, then the county may revoke the franchise or license and the
holder shall cease any solid waste service.
      (4)   The Board reserves the right to make further regulations as deemed
necessary to protect the welfare of the public.
   (E)   Amendments and adoption. When it is determined by the County Board of
Commissioners, whether or not as a result of a recommendation by the SWAC, that
this subchapter shall be amended, the amendment and adoption process will
follow the process outlined in Chapter 9 of the County Solid Waste Management
Plan.
(Ord. MC-03-06, passed 4-19-2006) Penalty, see §
51.99
**** TOXIC WASTE ****
§ 51.40 TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Toxic Waste
Ordinance.”
(Ord. MC-C-1-97, passed 3-5-1997)
§ 51.41 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PERSON. Any individual, corporation, partnership, association, municipal
entity, state government, federal government or any agency thereof.
   PUBLIC SAFETY OFFICER. A peace officer, county code enforcement officer,
fire prevention inspector, firefighter or any person who, during an emergency
formally declared by the County Board of Commissioners, has been deputized by
and is acting pursuant to the orders of the County Sheriff.
   TOXIC WASTE. Includes, but is not limited to, all “P-list” substances and
“F-list” substances defined by the State Department of Environmental Quality,
specifically:
      (1)   F998. Residues from demilitarization, treatment and testing of
blister agents (such as Mustard agent);
      (2)   F999. Residues from demilitarization, treatment and testing of
nerve agents (such as GB (Sarin) and VX);
      (3)   P998. Blister agents (such as Mustard agent); and
      (4)   P999. Nerve agents (such as GE (Sarin) and VX).
   TOXIC WASTE STORAGE UNIT. Any real property or construct thereon, including
tanks, barrels, silos, igloos or enclosure of any kind used, or intended for
use, for the storage of toxic waste.
   VEHICLE. Any device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be
transported or drawn upon a roadway, public or private and includes vehicles
that are propelled or powered by any means.
(Ord. MC-C-1-97, passed 3-5-1997)
§ 51.42 PROHIBITIONS.
   (A)   No person shall store, or permit to be stored, within the county any
toxic waste unless:
      (1)   A complete inventory of each kind, amount and location of such
toxic waste has been provided to the County Planning Department; and
      (2)   All storage fees, if any, imposed by the County Board of
Commissioners have been paid.
   (B)   No person shall transport, or permit to be transported, within the
county any toxic waste unless:
      (1)   A schedule of intended transport has been furnished to the County
Emergency Management Department, which schedule shall included the point of
departure, the intended destination, the kind and amount of waste to be
transported and the hours of transport within the county; or
      (2)   All transport fees, if any, imposed by the County Board of
Commissioners have been paid.
(Ord. MC-C-1-97, passed 3-5-1997) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.43 ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   Citations may be issued for violations of this chapter.
   (B)   In addition to other remedies provided by this subchapter, a violation
may be enjoined by a civil action pursuant to O.R.S. 30.315.
   (C)   In addition to other remedies provided by this subchapter, a violation
is hereby declared to be a nuisance, and may be regarded as such in all
actions, suits and proceedings.
(Ord. MC-C-1-97, passed 3-5-1997) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.44 JURISDICTION.
   This subchapter shall apply within those areas located inside the county
which are situated outside the city limits of an incorporated city. The
circuit, district and justice courts for the state for the county have
concurrent jurisdiction over any and all violations of this subchapter. In all
cases where civil penalty is sought to be imposed as provided in §
51.99, a complaint, signed by the County District Attorney or the county
counsel, shall be filed in the county justice court, which shall have original
jurisdiction over the proceedings. The proceedings shall thereafter be
conducted in accordance with the laws of the state and the rules of the county
justice court, including any right of appeal therefrom.
(Ord. MC-C-1-97, passed 3-5-1997)
§ 51.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   The county may enforce the provisions of §§
51.15 and
51.16 by administrative, civil or criminal proceedings or a combination
thereof, as necessary to achieve compliance. Further violation of this
subchapter may be punishable as a Class A misdemeanor under the provisions of
O.R.S. 459.992 and/or in addition thereof, a civil fine of up to $500 per day,
for each day of violation under the provisions of O.R.S. 459.995. The county
may also enforce the provisions of §
51.15 and 51.16 with the use of a lien as provided for herein.
   (C)   (1)   Any person who violates any provision of §
51.42 is guilty of a violation and may be issued a citation for the violation
which is punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.
      (2)   Any violation of any provision of §
51.42 which continues in duration for longer than 24 hours is a continuing
violation; a continuing violation is punishable by a fine not to exceed $1,000.
      (3)   Nothing herein shall prevent the county from treating each 24-hour
period of a continuing violation as a separate violation, prosecutable as such.
(Ord. MC-C-1-97, passed 3-5-1997)

**** ROAD WEIGHT LIMITS AND CLOSURES ****
§ 71.01 TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Weight Limit and
Closure Ordinance.”
(Prior Code, § 8.04.010) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.02 STATUTORY AUTHORITY.
   (A)   This subchapter is authorized under state law by O.R.S. 368.016, which
provides that the exercise of governmental powers relating to roads within a
county is a matter of county concern, and by O.R.S. 203.035, which grants to
counties the authority to enact ordinances governing matters of county concern.
   (B)   The County Board of Commissioners herein designates the exercise of
governmental powers relative to roads to be a matter of county concern to the
county.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.020) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.03 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COUNTY ROAD. A dedicated county road located outside an incorporated area.
It shall not include state highways.
   MOTOR VEHICLE. Any motor-driven method of conveyance, or farm implement,
including, but not limited to, automobiles, pickup trucks, trucks of any
nature, motorcycles or snowmobiles. MOTOR VEHICLE does not include county,
state or federal vehicles being used in the course of their public function,
ambulances or other emergency vehicles.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.030) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.04 LOAD LIMITS; IMPOSITION.
   The Roadmaster shall designate and maintain maximum weight limits for
vehicles traveling upon county roads. Such designation shall be made when, in
the judgment of the Roadmaster, weather conditions, atmospheric conditions,
surface conditions or other appropriate conditions are such that allowing
vehicles of greater weight to travel upon a county road would be detrimental to
vehicles, road surfaces, adjacent property or human beings, or would, in the
judgment of the Roadmaster, create such other detrimental condition sought to
be avoided.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.040) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.05 LOAD LIMITS; ROADMASTER POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   The Roadmaster is authorized to designate maximum weight limits at any
time, and without prior notice, and such designation shall carry the full force
and effect of law. However, the Roadmaster shall attend the next regularly
scheduled meeting of the County Board of Commissioners after a designation of
weight limit.
   (B)   At the County Board of Commissioners meeting, the Roadmaster shall
report all such designations. After such a report, the Roadmaster’s designation
shall be deemed to be ratified and adopted by the County Board of
Commissioners, unless contrary intention is expressed by the Board, at which
point the Roadmaster shall follow the direction of the Board.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.050) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.06 LOAD LIMITS; DETERMINATION FOR PROCEDURES.
   Section 71.11 notwithstanding, for the purpose of determining any gross
weight, actual scale weights shall govern. In the absence of information as to
scale weights or of convenient facilities for ascertaining scale weights, the
weights furnished by dealers, manufacturers or their agents or the weights
assigned to the particular vehicle by the state as the “light-weight” of the
vehicle, as to the weights of vehicles and parts of vehicles, and bills of
lading or cargo manifests as to weights of loads may be accepted as the weights
thereof, but such weights shall be subject at all times to verification by
actual weights subsequently ascertained.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.060) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.07 LOAD LIMITS; AVAILABLE FOR PUBLIC INSPECTION.
   (A)   (1)   At such time as the Roadmaster designates, a maximum weight
limit for a county road, he or she shall enter the following information into a
journal kept for that purpose:
         (a)   The road or portion of road so restricted;
         (b)   The maximum weight of vehicles for such road;
         (c)   The time and date upon which the restriction shall take effect;
and
         (d)   The duration of such restriction, which may or may not be
indefinite.
      (2)   Such journal shall be available for public inspection during
working hours at the County Public Works office in Lexington, Oregon.
   (B)   At such time as the Roadmaster designates a maximum weight limit for a
county road, he or she shall take the following steps to notify the public of
such restrictions.
      (1)   He or she shall notify all newspapers of general circulation within
the county of all information contained in division (A)(1) above.
      (2)   He or she shall notify any radio stations which serve the area
affected by the maximum weight designation of all information contained in
division (A)(1) above.
      (3)   He or she shall cause to be posted signs indicating the maximum
weight designation. Such signs shall be clearly readable highway-type signs and
shall display the maximum weight permitted; no other wording shall be
necessary. Signs shall be posted prominently at all points at which such county
road intersects with state or federal highways and at such other points as the
Roadmaster shall see fit.
   (C)   The Roadmaster may, at his or her discretion, give notice to
individual persons or business entities of any maximum weight designation, by
telephone or other suitable means, but he or she is not required to do so.
   (D)   Record shall be made of any notice given under divisions (B)(1)
through (B)(3) and (C) above, by entry in the journal provided for in division
(B)(1) above.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.070) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.08 ROAD CLOSURES.
   The Roadmaster is empowered to order that county roads be closed to motor
vehicle traffic. Except as may be specifically noted hereafter, all provisions
of this subchapter with reference to notice, enforcement, exemptions,
jurisdiction and penalties shall be applicable to road closures.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.080) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.09 EXEMPTIONS FROM COMPLIANCE; PERMIT REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   The Roadmaster is empowered to grant permits, which shall act as
temporary exemptions from compliance with maximum weight designations or
temporary closures authorized by this subchapter. Permits shall be available
from the Public Works Department office in Lexington, Oregon and shall be in
the form of a certificate. Permits shall indicate:
      (1)   To whom the permit applies;
      (2)   The duration of the permit;
      (3)   The road(s) to which the permit applies; and
      (4)   The degree to which the permit holder may exceed the maximum weight
and/or the extent to which the permit holder may travel upon a road which has
been temporarily closed.
   (B)   Other sections of this subchapter or the state statutes
notwithstanding, the Roadmaster, in his or her discretion, may permit an
overweight vehicle to travel upon a county road, or may allow a vehicle to
travel upon a closed road, in order to allow that vehicle to reach a roadway
upon which it would be a legally operating vehicle. Such discretionary
permission shall in no way affect the validity of a traffic citation issued in
that or any other instance.
   (C)   In the discretion of the County Board of Commissioners, a fee may be
charged for an exemption granted under this section. The amount of the fee
shall be by agreement between the Board and the applicant.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.090) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.10 LOAD LIMITS; STATUTORY LIMITS.
   In the absence of a maximum weight designation under this subchapter, weight
limits imposed by the state statutes shall be in effect. Enforcement mechanisms
provided in this subchapter shall be applicable to O.R.S.-prescribed weight
limits, and such weight limits shall be enforceable under this subchapter as a
county offense, except that the notice provisions of §§
71.04 through
71.07 shall not be required.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.100) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.11 ENFORCEMENT; STATUTORY AUTHORITY.
   Enforcement of this subchapter shall be as provided in O.R.S. 483.534,
483.536, 484.110 and by other relevant sections as applicable.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.110) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.12 LIABILITY FOR UNLAWFUL OPERATION.
   The operation of any vehicle or combination of vehicles in violation of this
subchapter is prima facie evidence that the owner of such vehicle or
combination caused or permitted it to be so operated, and the owner shall be
liable for any penalties imposed as a result of such operation.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.120) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984) Penalty, see §
71.99
§ 71.13 WEIGHMASTER.
   (A)   Appointment. The County Board of Commissioners shall appoint a person
to act as Weighmaster for the county, in whom shall reside all powers granted
to Weighmasters by this subchapter or by state statute.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.130)
   (B)   Deputies. The Weighmaster may appoint as Deputy Weighmasters those
persons that he or she may deem necessary. Appointments to the position of
Deputy Weighmaster shall not be effective until approved by the County Board of
Commissioners.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.140)
   (C)   Weighmaster and Deputy identification cards. The Weighmaster and
Deputy Weighmasters shall be issued identification cards identifying them as
empowered to enforce this subchapter and state weight and closure statutes. In
addition, the Weighmaster and Deputy Weighmasters shall carry copies of O.R.S.
483.534, 483.536, 483.991 and 484.110, although failure to do so shall not
constitute an avoidance or defense to uniform traffic citations issued under
this subchapter or state statutes.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.150)
(Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.14 ENFORCEMENT; CITATIONS.
   When, in accordance with state statute, the Weighmaster or Deputy
Weighmasters shall seek to enforce this subchapter or state statute with
reference to vehicle weight violations or road closure violations, they shall
do so by issuing a uniform traffic citation to the operator of the offending
vehicle. Such uniform traffic citation shall refer to this subchapter by its
short title.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.160) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
§ 71.15 CITATIONS; JURISDICTION.
   Concurrent jurisdiction over uniform traffic citations issued under this
subchapter shall rest with the county district court and the county justice
courts.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.170) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)
**** BRIDGE WEIGHT LIMITS ****
§ 71.30 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BRIDGE. All bridges constructed, owned or maintained by the county.
   GROSS WEIGHT. The whole weight of any weight of any motor vehicle or
combination of vehicles and its load.
(Prior Code, § 8.12.010) (Ord. passed 11-6-1963)
§ 71.31 WEIGHT LIMITS ON BRIDGES DESIGNATED.
   No person shall drive or move, and no owner shall cause or permit to be
driven or moved any vehicle or combination of vehicles with a combined weight
exceeding 20,000 pounds over or across any county-owned or county-maintained
bridge.
(Prior Code, § 8.12.020) (Ord. passed 11-6-1963) Penalty, see §
71.99
§ 71.32 EXEMPTIONS TO WEIGHT LIMITS.
   Section 71.31 does not apply to bridges that are a part of the state highway
system or federal interstate highway system, or so far as the provisions of
that section may be in conflict with O.R.S. Chapter 483 or 23 U.S.C. § 127.
(Prior Code, § 8.12.030) (Ord. passed 11-6-1963)
§ 71.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   (1)   Violation by any driver, chauffeur or owner of any vehicle or
combination of vehicles of the weight provisions of §§
71.01 through
71.15 is punishable, upon conviction, by a fine based upon the excess weight by
which any gross weight exceeds the applicable gross weight authorized, as
follows:
         (a)   Two thousand pounds or less, by a fine of not less than $15;
         (b)   More than 2,000 pounds, but not in excess of 3,000 pounds, by a
fine of not more than $0.01 per pound for each pound of the excess weight;
         (c)   More than 3,000 pounds, but not in excess of 5,000 pounds, by a
fine of not more than $0.02 per pound for each pound of the excess weight;
         (d)   More than 5,000 pounds, by a fine of not more than $0.07 per
pound for each pound of excess weight; and
         (e)   More than 7,500 pounds, by a fine of not more than $0.10 for
each pound of excess weight.
      (2)   Violation by any driver, chauffeur or owner or any vehicle or
combination of vehicles of the weight provisions of any permit issued under the
authority of §§
71.01 through
71.15 is punishable, upon conviction, by a fine of not more than $100, plus
$0.10 per pound for each pound by which any gross weight exceeds the applicable
gross weight authorized by the permit.
      (3)   In addition to the penalties provided in division (B) above, any
driver, chauffeur or owner of any vehicle who operates or permits to be
operated a motor vehicle in violation of a closure order issued pursuant to §
71.08 shall be subject to a fine, upon conviction, of up to $1,000.
(Prior Code, § 8.04.180) (Ord. MC-C-1-84, passed - -1984)

**** LIVESTOCK GRAZING; MULTIPLE-USE COMPLIANCE ****
§ 90.01 TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Multiple-Use
Compliance Ordinance.”
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.02 CRITERIA FOR DETERMINATION.
   Livestock grazing on public or private lands situated within the county
shall not, on the grounds that emergency conditions exist, be limited,
prohibited or made subject to regulation requiring substantial expenditure,
unless a written determination is obtained from the County Planning Director
(hereinafter referred to as “Director”), which determination is based upon
evidence sufficient to support the following findings:
   (A)   Serious resource damage is presently occurring;
   (B)   The damage is of a nature which is likely to produce effects beyond
the period of one grazing season;
   (C)   The damage is the result of actions or events not occurring naturally
on forest lands;
   (D)   The damage is directly attributable to livestock grazing; and
   (E)   No less burdensome alternative is reasonably available or practical.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.03 APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS.
   Any person, partnership, association, corporation or governmental agency
which owns or controls the use of forest lands may request a determination from
the Director that livestock grazing upon such lands situated in the county may
be limited, prohibited or made subject to regulation on the grounds that an
emergency exists upon an application providing all of the following
information:
   (A)   A specific description of the lands alleged to be affected by the
emergency;
   (B)   A specific description of the nature and effects of the emergency
alleged;
   (C)   A specific description of the resource or resources alleged to be
damaged, together with a description of the particular damage which is
occurring;
   (D)   The names and addresses of all persons whose livestock or other
property would be affected by the Director’s finding;
   (E)   All data which supports a finding that:
      (1)   The damage is of a nature which is likely to produce effects beyond
the period of one grazing season;
      (2)   The damage is the result of actions or events not occurring
naturally on forest lands; and
      (3)   The damage is directly attributable to livestock grazing.
   (F)   A detailed explanation of all facts which render any less burdensome
alternative unreasonable or impractical; and
   (G)   Any other information deemed necessary by the Director.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.04 NOTICE REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Except as set forth in division (B) below, upon receipt of an
application described in §
90.03, the Director shall, within three working days, send notice by registered
or certified mail to all persons whose livestock or other property may be
affected by the Director’s finding. The notice, with a copy of the application
attached, shall establish a time and place at which such person may appear and
be heard on the matter. The Director shall also notify the applicant of the
time and place of such hearing. The time set for said hearing shall be not less
than seven days or more than 14 days from the date upon which notice was sent
to the interested parties.
   (B)   If the Director determines that the information provided in the
application is inadequate or lacks sufficient specificity upon which to base a
determination, the Director shall notify the applicant of the particular
deficiency, in writing, within three days of receipt of the application. The
applicant shall have not more than 14 days to make such corrections or
additions to the application as the Director requires. If corrections or
additions to an application are deemed necessary, the Director shall not send
the notices required by division (A) above until the Director has approved the
application in final form.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.05 APPEAL.
   Any person aggrieved by the decision of the Director may appeal the decision
in the same manner and to the same extent as is provided by law for appeal of a
decision of the Director pursuant to the County Comprehensive Plan and Zoning
Ordinance.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.06 VENUE.
   This subchapter shall be applicable in the county and in all situations
which would establish venue for a criminal proceeding in the county under
O.R.S. 131.305 and 131.315.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.07 JURISDICTION.
   Jurisdiction and prosecution of offenses under this subchapter may be
initiated in either the justice court for the county or the district court for
the county; those courts having concurrent jurisdiction under this subchapter.
All other rules of procedure shall be as provided for other violation or
infraction prosecutions initiated in the respective court.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.08 CONFLICT WITH STATE LAW.
   Nothing in this subchapter shall be construed in such a way as to conflict
with state statutes or any other provision of law.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)
§ 90.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   No person shall order, authorize, require or otherwise effect the
removal of livestock from public or private forest lands situated within the
county, on the grounds that an emergency exists, other than an owner of such
livestock or a person acting at the direction of such owner, unless the person
has obtained the written determination of the Director as described in §
90.02. Any person who violates this provision, upon conviction, may be assessed
a fine not to exceed $500.
   (B)   No person shall knowingly assemble, create, gather, transmit or
present false, misleading or biased information or data in support of, or in
opposition to, a determination that serious resource damage is occurring, or
that an emergency exists, which requires the removal of livestock from forest
lands within the county. Any person who violates this provision, upon
conviction, may be assessed a fine not to exceed $500.
(Ord. MC-C-6-92, passed 7-29-1992)

§ 91.01 PARKS MASTER PLAN ADOPTED.

CHAPTER 92: AMBULANCE SERVICE PROVIDERS
Section
